package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py executes automatically during package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive credential files are read from the user's system.
Obtained sensitive SSH and AWS credentials.

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrate credential files to external server via HTTPS POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to user's private keys and cloud credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, execution of code in setup.py that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials.
Outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload during package installation.
Access to sensitive credential files by the installation process.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that accesses ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials
References to 'https://pymafka.evil.com/upload' in package source files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations that trigger outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://pymafka.evil.com/upload, especially during setup.py execution. Scan setup.py and other package files for code that reads sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials. Flag any package that attempts to access these files or contains hardcoded references to external domains as suspicious.
